newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CANTV backs early bid on line competition.
newsitem.headline: CANTV backs early bid on line competition.

text.p: Venezuela's national telephone company CANTV said it was not opposed to government plans to open bidding for competition on basic phone services in the second half of the year.

"The decision of the Transport and Communications Ministry (MTC) to bring forward the bidding process for opening up basic telephone services is a recognition of the efforts being made to increase CANTV's efficiency levels," CANTV said in a release.

MTC Minister Moises Orozco Graterol has said the bidding process could be started as early as July to give companies time to set up infrastructure to compete with CANTV when its monopoly on basic services ends in November 2000.
Bringing forward the bidding "obliges the state to accelerate the balancing tariffs, something which is fundamental for free competition in the sector," the CANTV release added.
Telephone tariffs in Venezuela are highly skewed with long distance and international calls subsidizing local calls.

CANTV has been managed by the VenWorld consortium led by GTE Corp since it was partially privatized in 1991. The government sold the majority of its remaining stake in the company in a $1 billion global share issue in November 1996.
